# CXNM - Standard - WIN - D - Wireless and Peripherals

Makes the device invisible over Bluetooth and shuts off Windows Connect Now, so that wireless settings cannot be transferred from one device to another outside management. Already paired devices keep working.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| Source | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.20 and A.7.9, NIS2 art. 21(2)(e) — settings from the IntuneAdmin Endpoint Security set |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Wireless_and_Peripherals.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Wireless_and_Peripherals.json) |

> Windows Connect Now is the forgotten route: with it, a user can transfer wireless settings — including the network password — via WPS or a USB stick from one device to another, outside any management. Both settings close that off. On the question of who can see each other's Wi-Fi profiles: profiles deployed via Intune or GPO are device-wide and therefore visible to every user of that device, and anyone who adds a network themselves can retrieve the associated password in plain text with netsh. As long as the corporate network runs on a shared password (PSK), every user who has ever connected therefore knows that password — no policy helps against that. The measure that does solve this is 802.1X with certificates, because then there is no shared secret to read out. Blocking manual Wi-Fi configuration altogether (AllowManualWiFiConfiguration) is deliberately left out: that makes working from home and hotels impossible, and teleworking should simply be possible. Stricter policies sometimes require all Bluetooth profiles except Serial Port Profile to be turned off. Implementing that literally breaks headphones, mice and keyboards; that first requires a decision. These four settings are the defensible intermediate step: the device can no longer be discovered or approached by a stranger, and existing pairings keep working. ServicesAllowedList is deliberately left out — it requires GUIDs per profile and, without a carefully compiled list, turns off more than intended.

## Settings — 6

Indented rows are child settings: they only apply when their parent
setting has the value shown.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `device_vendor_msft_policy_config_bluetooth_allowadvertising` | 0 |
| `device_vendor_msft_policy_config_bluetooth_allowdiscoverablemode` | 0 |
| `device_vendor_msft_policy_config_bluetooth_allowprepairing` | 0 |
| `device_vendor_msft_policy_config_bluetooth_allowpromptedproximalconnections` | 0 |
